sub.zh: 大卫与歌利亚 · 撒母耳记上 17 章

text.en: A man stops beside you. Dust on his clothes, a scribe's long robe. His name is Corin.
text.zh: 一个人在你身边停下。满身是土，穿文士的长袍。他叫柯林。

text.en: “This is the Valley of Elah. About 1020 years before Christ.”
text.zh: 「这里是以拉谷。算起来，是公元前一〇二〇年前后。」

text.en: “One thing to remember first: we are witnesses, not the ones this is about.”
text.zh: 「有一件事，你先记下：我们是见证人，不是主角。」

text.en: “The ending is God's; it is not ours to change. What is ours to decide is what kind of people we become.”
text.zh: 「结局是神定的，轮不到我们改。我们能定的，是自己要做什么样的人。」

text.en: Across the valley the Philistines shout their challenge every day. Forty days now.
text.zh: 山谷对面，非利士人天天叫阵。已经四十天了。

text.en: Not one man here has gone out.
text.zh: 这边没有一个人出去。

text.en: “So. Which side do you stand on?”
text.zh: 「那么，你站在哪一边？」

text.en: “Walk slowly. When you need me, I am here.”
text.zh: 「慢慢走。要用我的时候，我就在这儿。」

text.en: You came back.
text.zh: 你回来了。

text.en: “We all saw it. The boy went down without armour on.”
text.zh: 「我们都看见了。那孩子连甲都没穿，就下去了。」

text.en: “That last thing he said — did you keep it?”
text.zh: 「他最后说的那句话，你记住了吗？」

text.en: You did.
text.zh: 你记住了。

text.en: He holds his spear with both hands, head down.
text.zh: 他两手抱着矛，头低着。

text.en: “They say the fellow is three metres tall. Bronze from head to foot.”
text.zh: 「他们说那家伙有三米高，从头到脚都是铜。」

text.en: “His spear shaft is thicker than my arm.”
text.zh: 「他的枪杆，比我胳膊还粗。」

text.en: “I have never dared go close. I cannot see his face.”
text.zh: 「我没敢走近过。看不清他的脸。」

text.en: “The day I left, my mother said: do not be afraid.”
text.zh: 「我出门那天，我娘说：不要怕。」

text.en: “Then she cried before I did. She was afraid too, and she said it anyway.”
text.zh: 「说完她自己先哭了。她也怕，可她还是说了。」

text.en: “There is a line in the Law. The officers shout it at us every morning.”
text.zh: 「律法上有一句，官长天天冲我们喊。」

text.en: “Hear, O Israel, ye approach this day unto battle against your enemies:”
text.zh: 「以色列人哪，你们当听，你们今日将要与仇敌争战，

text.en: “let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them.”
text.zh: 不要胆怯，不要惧怕战兢，也不要因他们惊恐；」

text.en: “That is Deuteronomy, chapter twenty, verse three. I cannot say the whole of it. Only these lines.”
text.zh: 「这是《申命记》二十章三节。我记不全，就记得这几句。」

text.en: He pushes the words into your hand.
text.zh: 他把这句话塞进你手里。

text.en: “They are not mine. Take them.”
text.zh: 「不是我的。你拿着。」

text.en: “Go up if you have to. I will hold this spot.”
text.zh: 「你要上去就上去吧。这儿我守着。」

text.en: I climbed the ridge to look. Their tents are still standing. There is nobody inside them.
text.zh: 我爬上山脊去看。他们的帐棚还立着，里头一个人也没有。

text.en: You were aiming at his forehead. I saw the stone leave your hand. Just the once.
text.zh: 你是照着他的额头打的。我看见石头飞出去，就那么一下。

text.en: She is breaking bread. She does not look up.
text.zh: 她在分饼，头也没抬。

text.en: “You are going up too? My husband went up. He has not come down yet.”
text.zh: 「你也要上去？我男人上去了，到现在没下来。」

text.en: “I do not pray that he wins.”
text.zh: 「我不求他打赢。」

text.en: “Only that he does not leave his life up there.”
text.zh: 「只求他别把命丢在上头。」

text.en: “Take this. Bread, and a word with it.”
text.zh: 「拿着。饼，还有一句话。」

text.en: “Bread will not keep until tomorrow. The word will carry you further.”
text.zh: 「饼搁不到明天。这句话，能陪你走得远些。」

text.en: “Eat something before you climb. Nobody fights well empty.”
text.zh: 「上去以前先吃口东西。空着肚子，仗打不好。」

text.en: I had the water boiling for the wounded. They came back with no wounds at all, and none of them could stand.
text.zh: 我把水烧上了，等伤兵回来。回来的人一个伤也没有，却站都站不住。

text.en: Someone carried the giant's armour into one of the tents. Nobody will sleep in that one tonight.
text.zh: 有人把那巨人的甲抬进了一顶帐棚。今晚没人肯睡那一顶。

text.en: An old man sits by the road, mending a strap.
text.zh: 一个老人坐在路边，修一条皮带。

text.en: “They will not let you through.”
text.zh: 「他们不会放你过去的。」

text.en: “The king says it too: you are too young, and the man has soldiered since he was a boy.”
text.zh: 「王也是这个话：你年纪太轻，人家自小就当兵。」

text.en: “He says you are young. He is not wrong about that.”
text.zh: 「他说你年轻——这话没说错。」

text.en: “His mistake is thinking that young means worth nothing.”
text.zh: 「他错在以为，年轻就什么都不是。」

text.en: “All my life, people have looked me up and down and settled on a price.”
text.zh: 「我这一辈子，都是这样被人上上下下看的。」

text.en: He pulls the strap one hole tighter.
text.zh: 他把皮带又勒紧一格。

text.en: “Carry one sentence back with you. Let him speak, and have your answer ready.”
text.zh: 「带一句话回去。他开口，你答得上。」

text.en: “The stones are at the brook, downstream past the tents. He took five. Not six.”
text.zh: 「石子在下游溪边，过了帐篷就是。他拿了五块，不是六块。」

text.en: Forty days he stood there and cursed us. I counted every one of them, the way a man counts his own grave.
text.zh: 四十天，他天天站在那儿骂我们。我一天天数，像数着自己的坟。

text.en: They ran them all the way to Gath and Ekron. I am too old to keep up, so I wait here for news.
text.zh: 他们一路追到迦特和以革伦去了。我老了，跟不动，就在这儿等消息。

text.en: “Hear, O Israel, ye approach this day unto battle against your enemies: let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them.”
text.zh: 「以色列人哪，你们当听，你们今日将要与仇敌争战，不要胆怯，不要惧怕战兢，也不要因他们惊恐；」

text.en: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.”
text.zh: 「你来攻击我，是靠着刀枪和铜戟；我来攻击你，是靠着万军之耶和华的名，就是你所怒骂带领以色列军队的神。」

text.en: “for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.”
text.zh: 「耶和华不像人看人：人是看外貌，耶和华是看内心。」

text.en: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
text.zh: 「耶和华是我的牧者，我必不致缺乏。」

triggers.note: the witness's first clear look at the giant (a camera shot, not a wall)

text.en: The ridge is low here, and the far slope is suddenly not far at all. You see him properly for the first time.
text.zh: 这道矮脊很低，对面的坡忽然一点也不远了。你这才第一次看清他。

text.en: Bronze helmet, bronze coat, bronze on his legs, and a spear like a weaver's beam. He does not raise his voice; both valleys hear him anyway.
text.zh: 铜盔、铜甲、腿上也是铜，一根枪杆粗得像织布的轴。他不用提高声音，两边山谷都听得见。

text.en:
1 Samuel 17:10
“And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:10
「那非利士人又说：我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我战斗。」

text.en: Nobody moves. Not one man on this side of the valley takes a step forward.
text.zh: 没有人动。谷这边，没有一个人往前迈一步。

text.en: Now you have seen him. That is what the last forty days have been. We watch. We do not go up.
text.zh: 「现在你看见他了。这四十天，就是这件事。我们看着，不上去。」

triggers.note: crossing north of this row as the witness: refused until the camp has explained itself, then the story changes hands (BECOME)

text.en: You step over the line. Two soldiers turn, and one of them walks you back with the flat of his spear.
text.zh: 你跨过那条线。两个兵转过身来，其中一个用枪杆把你推回去。

text.en: Not yet. You do not even know what you are looking at.
text.zh: 「还早。你连自己看的是什么都不知道。」

text.en: Forty days. A man shouts across the valley, and an army stands still. Somebody in this camp can tell you why.
text.zh: 四十天。有人隔着山谷叫阵，一支军队站着不动。营里总有人能告诉你为什么。

text.en: The line is still in the dust. Your hand still remembers the weight of five stones.
text.zh: 尘土里那条线还在。你的手还记得五块石子的重量。

text.en: You do not have to fight him again. You only have to remember that you stood here.
text.zh: 你不用再打他一次。你只要记得：你曾经站在这里。

text.en: You step over the line in the dust. Nobody stops you this time, and that is what frightens you.
text.zh: 你跨过尘土里那条线。这一次没有人拦你——让你发慌的正是这个。

text.en:
1 Samuel 17:11
“When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:11
「扫罗和以色列众人听见非利士人的这些话，就惊惶，极其害怕。」

text.en: You came to see this. You did not come to end it.
text.zh: 「你是来看这件事的。你不是来结束它的。」

text.en: Somebody else is already walking into the valley with bread in his hands. The story is about to change hands.
text.zh: 「另一个人已经提着饼，正往谷里走。故事要换到别人手上了。」

text.en: The valley folds. Three days ago, in the south, a father has just called a boy in from the sheep.
text.zh: 山谷合拢起来。三天前，南边，一个父亲刚把放羊的儿子叫回家。

text.en: You are a pilgrim. You came into the Valley of Elah behind the army of Israel.
text.zh: 你是个朝圣者。你跟着以色列的军队，走进了以拉谷。

text.en: The battle is not yours. All you can do is walk this valley and listen to its people.
text.zh: 这一仗不是你的。你能做的，只是走完这段路，听这里的人说话。

text.en: Keep whatever they give you. On the day, you will not only watch David. You will be him.
text.zh: 他们交给你的话，你要带上。到了那一天，你不会只是看着大卫——你会成为他。

text.en: Left thumb on the left half of the screen: walk. Push further out: run. A, bottom right: talk.
text.zh: 左手拇指按住画面左半边：走。推远一点：跑。右下角的 A：跟人说话。

text.en: Tap the screen to go on. If you lose the way, follow the arrow at the top right.
text.zh: 点一下画面，往下翻。找不到路，就看右上角的箭头。

stones.en: Five smooth stones. Five — not six for luck, and no sword.
stones.zh: 挑五块光滑的石子。五块——不多带一块讨吉利，也不带刀。

line.en: Walk up to the line. The whole army is watching.
line.zh: 走上去，走到界线那里。全军都在看着。

done.en: Chapter complete · the valley is quiet now
done.zh: 本章完成 · 山谷安静了

provision.en: Pick up the three things your father gave you
provision.zh: 把父亲给的三样东西拿上

brothers.en: Walk to the edge of the camp. Your brothers are there
brothers.zh: 走到营地边上。哥哥们在那边

fight.en: Dodge his spear. Then put a stone in his forehead. Three of them.
fight.zh: 躲开他的枪。然后把石子打进他的额头，三次。

npc.en: Walk with Corin. He will bring you to %s.
npc.zh: 跟着柯林走。他带你去找%s。

shepherd.en: A stone in the pouch. Practise on the jars.
shepherd.zh: 皮兜里放一块石子，对着陶罐练手。

saul.en: Hear the king out. Then go.

ready.en: Walk to the line. The whole army is watching.
ready.zh: 走到界线那里。全军都在看着你。

aftermath.en: Corin is waiting to hear it from you.
aftermath.zh: 柯林在等你，把话讲给他听。

line_witness.en: Walk to the line in the dust. Forty days, and no one has gone up.
line_witness.zh: 走到尘土里那条界线。四十天，没有一个人上去。

refused.en: You have not understood yet what you are watching. Talk to the people in the camp.
refused.zh: 你还没看明白，这四十天里到底是什么事。去和营地的人说话。

brook.en: Go down to the brook. Five smooth stones, and you choose them.
brook.zh: 下到溪边去。五块光滑的石子，由你自己挑。

firstsight.en: Get a look at the man shouting across the valley
firstsight.zh: 看一眼那个隔着山谷叫阵的人

armour.en: Walk in the king's armour. You will find out why it has to come off.
armour.zh: 穿着王的盔甲走走吧。你会知道它为什么非脱下来不可。

text.en: The battle is the LORD's.
text.zh: 争战的胜败在乎耶和华。

text.en: The stone was not thrown by your hand. But you learned one thing: do not stare at the giant in front of you.
text.zh: 石子不是你扔的。可你学会了一件事：不要只盯着眼前的巨人。

text.en: Look at the God who is greater than he is.
text.zh: 要看那位比巨人更大的神。

text.en: Remember the road God has already walked you down. That is where courage for this one comes from.
text.zh: 回头看看，神是怎么一路带你走过来的。你才有勇气，面对眼前这一个。

text.en: Faith does not arrive all at once. It grows each time you look back.
text.zh: 信心不是突然长出来的。是一次一次回头看，慢慢长出来的。

ask.en: What giant is standing in front of you now? What would your first step of faith be?
ask.zh: 你生命里，现在站着什么样的巨人？信心的第一步，你想怎么走？

t.en: Remember the road God has already walked me through
t.zh: 先回想神带我走过的路

insight.en: That is how David began — not with the giant, but with the lion and the bear behind him. (1 Samuel 17:37)
insight.zh: 大卫就是从这儿开始的。不是从巨人开始，是从身后的狮子和熊开始。（撒母耳记上 17:37）

t.en: Say it out loud to someone

insight.en: That is wisdom. Before David went down to the giant, he was already talking to the men in the line. (1 Samuel 17:26)
insight.zh: 这是聪明人的走法。下阵以前，大卫也先跟阵上的人说过话。（撒母耳记上 17:26）

t.en: Take off armour that is not mine

insight.en: Saul's armour was good. It was only not David's. Discernment is knowing which help is actually yours. (1 Samuel 17:39)
insight.zh: 扫罗那副盔甲是好的，只是它不是大卫的。分辨，就是分得清哪一份帮助真是给你的。（撒母耳记上 17:39）

text.en: You look down. These hands are not yours.
text.zh: 你低下头。眼前这双手，不是你的。

text.en: Three days earlier. Bethlehem.
text.zh: 三天前。伯利恒。

text.en: Your father stands in the doorway with a cloth bag in his hand.
text.zh: 父亲站在门口，手里提着一只布袋。

text.en: “Take this to your brothers: bread, cheese, and parched grain.”
text.zh: 「把这个给你哥哥们带去：饼、奶酪，还有炒好的麦子。」

text.en: “They are with Saul's army, in the Valley of Elah. Go and see whether they are well.”
text.zh: 「他们跟着扫罗的军队，在以拉谷。去看看他们好不好。」

text.en: Pick up what your father has given you. Three things.
text.zh: 把父亲给的东西拿上。一共三样。

text.en: Your eldest brother sees you coming up the road.
text.zh: 长兄看见你走上坡来。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:28
text.zh: 撒母耳记上 17:28

text.en: “Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness?”
text.zh: 「你下来做什么？在旷野的那几只羊，你交托了谁呢？」

text.en: “I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.”
text.zh: 「我知道你的骄傲和你心里的恶意；你下来特为要看争战。」

text.en: You say nothing. Someone leads you into the king's tent.
text.zh: 你什么也没说。有人领你进了王的帐棚。

text.en: Three days earlier. The slope south of Bethlehem.
text.zh: 三天前。伯利恒南边的坡上。

text.en: The sheep graze behind you. The sling in your hand is worn shiny by your palm.
text.zh: 羊在背后吃草。机弦握在手里，被手心磨得发亮。

text.en: A row of clay jars stands on the slope. You throw at them every day until your arm aches.
text.zh: 坡上立着一排陶罐。你天天对着它们扔石头，扔到胳膊发酸。

text.en: This is not battle. This is practice.
text.zh: 这不是打仗。是练手。

text.en: The last jar breaks. Someone below the slope is calling your name.
text.zh: 最后一只罐子也碎了。坡下有人喊你的名字。

text.en: Your father wants you at the camp. Your brothers are there.
text.zh: 父亲叫你去一趟军营。哥哥们在那边。

text.en: Saul stands a head taller than every man in the tent.
text.zh: 扫罗比帐棚里所有人都高出一头。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:33 — “And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:33
「扫罗对大卫说：你不能去与那非利士人战斗；因为你年纪太轻，他自幼就作战士。」

text.en: “The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”
text.zh: 「耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。」

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:37 — “Go, and the LORD be with thee.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:37
「你可以去吧！耶和华必与你同在。」

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:38 — “And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:38
「扫罗就把自己的战衣给大卫穿上，将铜盔给他戴上，又给他穿上铠甲。」

text.en: The line is behind you now. He has been waiting forty days for somebody to come down.
text.zh: 界线就在你身后。他等一个人下来，已经等了四十天。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:44 — “And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:44
「非利士人又对大卫说：来吧！我将你的肉给空中的飞鸟、田野的走兽吃。」

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:45 — “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield:
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:45
「你来攻击我，是靠着刀枪和铜戟；

text.en: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.”
text.zh: 我来攻击你，是靠着万军之耶和华的名，就是你所怒骂带领以色列军队的神。」

text.en: You set a stone in the sling. Five of them, warm in your hand.
text.zh: 你把一块石子扣进皮兜。五个石子，在你手心里。

text.en: The stone sinks into his forehead. Goliath falls face down into the dust he cursed for forty days.
text.zh: 石子陷进他的额头。歌利亚脸朝下，扑倒在他骂了四十天的那片尘土里。

text.en: The Philistine line breaks at once. The whole army of Israel shouts as one.
text.zh: 非利士人的阵线一下子散了。以色列全军在同一刻喊了出来。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:47 — “And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’S, and he will give you into our hands.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:47
「又使这众人知道耶和华使人得胜，不是用刀用枪，因为争战的胜败全在乎耶和华。他必将你们交在我们手里。」

text.en: This was never the story of a small boy beating a big man.
text.zh: 这从来不是「小男孩打败大巨人」的故事。

text.en: It is the story of a God who keeps covenant, and a boy who knew the battle was not his.
text.zh: 这是一位守约的神，和一个知道这场仗不属于自己的少年。

text.en: Five stones in the bag, and the bag is light. Your sling is in your other hand.
text.zh: 五块石子在袋里，袋子轻得几乎没有分量。另一只手里，是你从少年时就带着的机弦。

text.en: Not armour. Not a sword. This.
text.zh: 「不是盔甲。不是刀。是这个。」

text.en: The armour is behind you on the tent floor. The brook runs shallow and cold between the stones.
text.zh: 盔甲留在身后的帐棚里。溪水从石头缝里流过，又浅又凉。

text.en: You crouch and turn the wet stones over with your fingers. Most of them are wrong — too sharp, too big, no weight to them.
text.zh: 你蹲下去，用手指把湿石头一块一块翻过来。大多都不合适：太尖、太大，或者拿在手里一点分量也没有。

text.en: Pick five. Not a handful — five.
text.zh: 挑五块。不是抓一把——是五块。

text.en:
1 Samuel 17:40
“And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook,
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:40
「他手中拿杖，又在溪中挑选了五块光滑石子，

text.en: and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip;
text.zh: 放在袋里，就是牧人带的囊里；

text.en: and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.”
text.zh: 手中拿着甩石的机弦，就去迎那非利士人。」

text.en: The coat of mail settles on your shoulders and the helmet comes down over your eyes. Everything you are wearing belongs to a man twice your size.
text.zh: 锁子甲压在肩上，铜盔扣下来，遮住了眉毛。你身上穿的，每一件都属于一个比你大一倍的人。

text.en: Walk. He is watching, and so is everyone outside the tent.
text.zh: 走两步。他看着你，帐外的人也都看着。

text.en: Two steps and the weight takes your knees. You catch yourself on the tent pole.
text.zh: 才两步，那分量就把你的腿压弯了。你扶住帐棚的杆子才没摔倒。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:39 — “I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them.”
text.zh:
撒母耳记上 17:39
「我穿戴这些不能走，因为素来没有穿惯。」

text.en: The bronze comes off piece by piece. The camp is quieter than it was when you put it on.
text.zh: 铜甲一件一件卸下来。你穿上它的时候，营里比现在吵。

text.en: What is left is a sling, a staff, and the clothes you came up the hill in.
text.zh: 剩下的是一条机弦、一根手杖，和你上山时穿的那身衣服。

text.en: You fell asleep on the bus home.
text.zh: 你在回家的车上睡着了。

text.en: You open your eyes. The sun is straight overhead and your mouth is full of dust.
text.zh: 再睁眼，日头正当头，嘴里满是土。

text.en: The clothes are not yours: coarse wool, scratching at your neck, a leather cord at the waist.
text.zh: 身上的衣服不是你的：粗羊毛，磨得脖子发痒，腰间一条皮绳。

text.en: There are armies on both ridges. Nobody moves. Nobody makes a sound.
text.zh: 两边的山脊上都站着军队。没有人动，也没有人出声。

text.en: Behind you, someone is crying quietly. You understand every word he says.
text.zh: 身后有人在低声哭。他说的每一个字，你都听得懂。

text.en: The brook is shallow and cold. The stones have been worn smooth.
text.zh: 溪水又浅又凉。石子被水磨得没有棱角。

text.en: A few stones stacked into an altar. The altar is cold; nobody has offered anything here in a long while.
text.zh: 几块石头垒成一座坛。坛是冷的——好些日子没人献过祭了。

text.en: The trunk is scored with knife marks. Men come here for firewood, and men come here to hide.
text.zh: 树干上有一道道刀痕。有人来砍柴，也有人来躲。

text.en: Inside the tent someone is bent over, stitching hide. If there is to be a battle, somebody has to mend what is torn.
text.zh: 帐棚里有人低头缝皮子。要打仗，也总得有人先把破的地方补上。
